thread.title: Twilio: A Tech Stock On The Rise - Twilio (NYSE:TWLO)

author: TipRanks
title: Twilio: A Tech Stock On The Rise - Twilio (NYSE:TWLO)
text:
The cloud communications Platform as a Service company Twilio, Inc. (NYSE: TWLO ) has made waves in recent weeks, with news breaking in October that it would acquire email marketing platform SendGrid, Inc. (NYSE: SEND ) in a $2 billion stock deal, followed by Q3 earnings that surpassed expectations. Twilio stock surged $25 - a hefty 35% - after the Nov. 6 Q3 report.
In detail, the Q3 results showed a revenue beat of $18.5 million, or 12%. Total revenue was $168.9 million and the forward guidance for Q4 of $161.4 million, both also well above expectations. The SendGrid deal was also seen as a net positive, in that it will combine two proven online communication systems. Sameer Dholakia, CEO of SendGrid, emphasized this when he told Reuters, "A huge part of the calculus for both sides was the cross-sell opportunity." Dholakia will continue to lead SendGrid as a stand-alone subsidiary of Twilio.
An Advantageous Acquisition The two companies expect to complete the acquisition during the first half of calendar year 2019. At that time, Twilio take full ownership of SendGrid, and SendGrid's common stock will convert to Twilio shares. With Twilio shares priced at $91, and SendGrid's at $44, the deal looks to strongly favor SendGrid's investors. The companies are forecasting more than $700 million in annual revenue after the acquisition, however, so the deal looks like it will pay for itself within three years.
All in all, this acquisition looks like the right move from the investor perspective. Twilio CEI Jeff Lawson set the tone, saying the day of the announcement,
"We believe this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to bring together the two leading developer-focused communications platforms to create the unquestioned platform of choice for all companies looking to transform their customer engagement."
From the SendGrid side, the acquisition deal is acclaim from market analysts. David Gearhart ( Track Record & Ratings ) of First Analysis points out that "combining Twilio and SendGrid, with their respective leadership positions in text and email communication, is a 'logical move.' Investors are best served holding SendGrid shares through the anticipated first half of 2019 exchange." At that point, the shares will convert to TWLO, with a market price just over double that of SEND.
Catching up to the Target Price Turning to market performance, TWLO has taken a hit with the recent market downturn despite the good news of the SendGrid deal. At the same time, the strong Q3 shielded Twilio from the body blow that afflicted less fortunate companies. Twilio has regained 21% from its recent bottom and now stands at $91 per share. The average target price of $99 represents just an 8% upside potential, but that is due to the stock catching up with the target price rather than any weakness. Share prices of TWLO are up 264% over the last 12 months. The stock holds a 'Strong Buy' consensus, based on 12 recent 'buy' ratings and zero 'hold' or 'sell' ratings.
View TWLO Price Target & Analyst Ratings Detail
Analysts and Bloggers Give Rave Reviews One of those 'buy' ratings came from Oppenheimer's Ittai Kidron ( Track Record & Ratings ). He cites the SendGrid deal specifically when he says of TWLO that he "continues to see strong core business upside and compelling SendGrid deal rationale/synergies." Kidron is bullish on the stock; his target price of $110 is an aggressive 20% over the current share value.
Twilio is getting bullish reviews from bloggers, as well. Rick Munarriz ( Track Record & Ratings ) makes a typical comment when he says,
"The top provider of in-app communications solutions has had a great year, and things just keep getting better for the stock that has nearly quadrupled in 2018. Revenue growth is accelerating, going from a 41% year-over-year pop in the fourth quarter of last year to advances of 48% in the first quarter, 54% in the second quarter, to a blistering 68% pop the last time out."
Munarriz has a 14% average return when recommending Twilio stock.
A Bright Spot for Tech The interwebs have been full of bad news about tech sector stocks in recent months. We all know by now how the sharp decline of the FAANG (Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ), Netflix (NASDAQ: NFLX ), Google (Alphabet) (NASDAQ: GOOG ) (NASDAQ: GOOGL )) stocks has led the general market decline, and the outlook for tech - at least in the short run - is cloudy. Twilio presents us with a completely different message: a tech stock that's rising, bucking the market trends to bring solid returns for investors. And even better, it shows no sign of being a 'flash in the pan.' With strong earnings, and an acquisition deal set to boost revenues, Twilio is definitely showing growth potential in difficult market environment.
Author: Michael Marcus
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
